title: Stop Overthinking in 60 Seconds: A Biblical Reset
hook: Mind won’t stop? Do this in 60 seconds.
script: Mind won’t stop? Do this in 60 seconds. I used to spiral at night: What if I fail? What if God is silent? Here’s the reset. One, breathe deep and name the fear out loud. Two, separate fact from feeling through Philippians 4:8—what is true, noble, right, pure? Three, reframe the thought with Scripture: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. Four, surrender the outcome in prayer: Father, I cast this on You because You care for me. Five, take one obedient micro-action you can do today. Peace grows in motion. Save this and repeat when the spiral starts.

title: 5-Step Bible Countdown for Racing Thoughts
script: You may be overthinking this. Try a 5-to-1 reset. Five slow breaths while you name the worry. Four lines between facts and feelings using Philippians 4:8 to test what’s true. Three truths to replace the lie: God is with me (Isaiah 41:10), God is good (Psalm 34:8), God will guide me (Proverbs 3:5-6). Two minutes to surrender: Lord, Your will, not mine; I cast this on You (1 Peter 5:7). One small step of obedience today. Don’t solve tomorrow; Jesus said, do not worry about it (Matthew 6:34). Replay this whenever your thoughts start to race.

title: The PEACE Method: 5 Biblical Steps to Quiet the Spiral
hook: If you're feeling anxious, watch this.
script: If you're feeling anxious, watch this. Use the PEACE method to stop the spiral. P: Pause and breathe; name the fear to the Lord. E: Examine the thought with Philippians 4:8—does it match what is true and pure? A: Anchor it to Scripture; take the thought captive with 2 Corinthians 10:5 and declare Isaiah 26:3 over your mind. C: Commit the outcome to God in prayer; He cares for you. E: Execute one tiny, faithful step. Text the person, send the email, or simply go for a five-minute walk. Save this and use PEACE anytime the noise gets loud.
